opus.why: Ledger reconciliation: an anti-join query plus a check of the hypothesis against provider_callbacks. It's money data, so edge cases matter (timeouts that later succeed, ledger rows not linked to a request), but this is well-scoped SQL reasoning.

fable.why: Financial-integrity diagnosis: needs a correct read-only anti-join plus reasoning about timeout/callback timing before confirming the hypothesis. Sonnet at high effort handles schema-level SQL and this causal check without loss; Opus adds nothing here.

opus.why: Small CSV. Group averages and a simple weekly trend, which a short script computes reliably. Terse output was requested.

fable.why: Twelve-row CSV, group averages and a weekly trend eyeball, terse Russian answer. Haiku with a quick script gets the numbers right; medium keeps it from skipping the actual computation.

opus.why: Trivial arithmetic: a percentage and month-over-month growth.

fable.why: Two arithmetic operations (27.2%, +21.4%). Trivial, no tools needed.

opus.why: Routine matplotlib grouped bar chart with set colors and a reusable script. Needs clean, client-presentable output, but no deep reasoning.

fable.why: Standard matplotlib grouped-bar chart with specified brand hex colors, PNG output and reusable script. Well-specified, moderate visual care; Sonnet medium produces clean, correct code and a presentable chart.

opus.why: Extends the earlier query with grouping by month and plan type plus a trend read. Standard SQL; the one thing to catch is that the most recent month is incomplete.

fable.why: Extends an existing Postgres CTE with month grouping and plan split, then reads the trend. Routine SQL extension plus short interpretation; Sonnet medium is sufficient.

opus.why: Swap the looping pairwise stats for a vectorized df.corr or a feature-importance approach, and judge whether the step is needed at all. Routine data-engineering call.

fable.why: Replace a slow bootstrap pairwise loop with vectorized pandas corr (or drop it) and advise whether it's needed. Judgment call but a standard one; Sonnet medium answers quickly and correctly.

opus.why: Cohort retention SQL with fiddly edge cases (multiple bookings in the first week, week offsets, pivot-ready output). Needs care to get right, but it's well specified.

fable.why: Cohort retention SQL with explicit edge cases (completed-only, first-week repeat bookings not counted, pivot-ready output). Correctness of date bucketing and the exclusion rule needs careful reasoning, which Sonnet at high effort delivers.

opus.why: Goes to a client tomorrow. With n=20 and tiny age segments, it takes careful statistical judgment (choosing the right test, multiple comparisons, saying plainly that segments are noise) and honest framing. Overclaiming would cost the most here.

fable.why: Client-facing tomorrow: overall and per-segment winner plus honest significance judgment on n=20 (chi-square/Friedman, underpowered subgroups). Needs sound stats and careful framing; Sonnet high is reliable here without needing Opus.

opus.why: Conceptual data-feasibility question plus a plan update, no queries. Needs a look at the events schema and sound reasoning about churn definitions.

fable.why: Planning-only question: inspect events schema, reason whether churn is derivable without billing data, update the plan. No code to write; Sonnet medium gives a correct, well-reasoned assessment.
